subject: Urgent: Pegasus Bank - Post-upgrade latency & error surge (exec bridge requested)
messages:
From: Elena Santos <elena.santos@pegasusbank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>; Victor Lau <victor.lau@pegasusbank.com>
Cc: procurement@pegasusbank.com
Date: Mon, 10 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate: high latency + 5xx after model upgrade

Irene / Redwood team,

We completed the model update you pushed last night (v5.4 with the new int8 quant profile). Since ~03:20 UTC we've seen a sharp increase in average latency (p95 from ~210ms to ~1.2s) and a spike in 5xxs across our production inference path. This is impacting customer-facing flows (loan-eligibility checks) and our queues are backing up.

We attached a screenshot of the Grafana board and a short error log excerpt (pegasus_kpi_screenshot.png, pegasus_error_log_0910.txt). Our ops team has throttled non-critical routes but the core path remains degraded.

Can you escalate? Our COO is on standby and will join an exec bridge if needed. Requesting immediate rollback or mitigation steps.

— Elena
Elena Santos
Head of Platform Engineering, Pegasus Bank
elena.santos@pegasusbank.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Sep 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: high latency + 5xx after model upgrade

Team —

Thanks Elena for the heads up and the artifacts. This looks like the int8 profile we rolled yesterday behaved badly on their hotpath (long sequences + attention pattern). Need immediate triage. Proposed immediate actions:

- Stand up an urgent exec bridge (Irene, Ben, Marissa, SEs, and Pegasus engineering).
- Temporarily route Pegasus hotpath to v5.3 fp16 variant (fast rollback path exists).
- Capture a KV-cache trace and full request IDs for 03:00–04:00 UTC.
- Run a quick latency profile on dedicated pool to reproduce p95 spike.

Ben — can you own rollback and memory/throughput checks? Marissa — please coordinate comms and prep a brief for the bridge (customer impact, SLA exposure, ask). Karthik — ops primers: are there any downstream throttles or batching policy changes that might amplify this?

I'll schedule a 30-minute bridge now (invite + agenda attached).

Irene Choi
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: bridge_agenda.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Immediate: high latency + 5xx after model upgrade

On Mon, Sep 10, 2028 at 09:22 Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team —
>
> Thanks Elena for the heads up and the artifacts. This looks like the int8 profile we rolled yesterday behaved badly on their hotpath (long sequences + attention pattern). Need immediate triage. Proposed immediate actions:
>
> - Stand up an urgent exec bridge (Irene, Ben, Marissa, SEs, and Pegasus engineering).
> - Temporarily route Pegasus hotpath to v5.3 fp16 variant (fast rollback path exists).
> - Capture a KV-cache trace and full request IDs for 03:00–04:00 UTC.
> - Run a quick latency profile on dedicated pool to reproduce p95 spike.

I am initiating the rollback to v5.3 on the Pegasus dedicated pool now (will keep the canary route live until we confirm). Rolling steps I'm running:

1) Drain new-int8 pool (safe-shutdown, preserve logs).
2) Re-route traffic via routing policy (latency-first) to fp16 v5.3 (expected < 10m to shift).
3) Run immediate load test to validate restored p95.
4) Persist evidence artifacts to shared Drive folder and tag OPS-3312.

I've attached a short error excerpt I pulled (pegasus_error_log_0910.txt). Initial observation: a decode stall pattern at ~token 128 for long prompts when quantized kernels fall back to slower fallback loops. This matches an internal regression we saw in staging for a very particular prompt length distribution.

I'll post updates to the bridge. If rollback restores SLA we propose a hotfix: re-profile kernels for Pegasus-specific prompt mix and add a canary window before global int8 rollouts.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pegasus_error_log_0910.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Elena Santos <elena.santos@pegasusbank.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Sep 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: high latency + 5xx after model upgrade

Bridge summary for execs (draft):

- Impact: Pegasus production loan checks p95 increased from ~210ms -> ~1.2s; error rate rose from 0.2% -> 3.8% starting 03:20 UTC; estimated customer-facing transactions impacted ~2.3k/min at peak. Potential SLA violations if >30m.
- Immediate remediation: Ben initiating rollback to v5.3 fp16; expect traffic normalization within 12–15 minutes after routing shift.
- Root cause (prelim): quantized int8 kernels triggered fallback path on long sequences (prompt length distribution on Pegasus hotpath not covered by current perf profile).
- Asks: exec approval for a targeted credit (contract clause) given measurable downtime window; commit to a Pegasus-specific re-profiling and a controlled canary before next int8 rollouts.

Irene — please confirm if you want legal/finance on the bridge (Pegasus already looped procurement). Sean — can you prepare the CX note for the COO?

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Elena —

Thanks for surfacing this. We just completed the routing change and early telemetry shows p95 returning to ~230ms and 5xxs dropping back toward baseline. We'll keep the bridge open for 2 hours to validate.

On the credit ask: I propose we offer a service credit for the 30-minute exposure window and follow up with a joint post-mortem and remediation plan. Legal/finance will need the exact timestamps and affected volumes — Marissa will coordinate.

Agenda for the next 90 minutes on the bridge:
- Confirm full traffic normalization (Ben)
- Share log artifacts + KV traces (Ops)
- Walkthrough re-profiling plan and timeline (Engineering)
- Agree on credits & comms (CS + Finance)

— Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Operations
Redwood Inference
